notes:
Summary: TidalFlow builds a real-time logistics assistant and large-scale embedding index for routing and docs. They require deterministic performance and strong locality for EU customers.

Primary asks:
- Firm dedicated capacity with active-active behavior across US-EAST and EU-CENTRAL, warm standby in APAC.
- P95 latency SLOs for chat generation <= 160ms; P99 objectives for critical routing calls <= 350ms.
- Capacity planning must include multi-AZ loss scenarios and cross-region failover headroom (they requested modeled scenarios at 20%, 30%, and 50% headroom).
- Explicit definition of burst vs reserved vs preemptible capacity for billing.

Traffic profile and constraints:
- Typical day: 300 concurrent chat sessions during peak across regions (US 60%, EU 30%, APAC 10%).
- Average turn: 180 tokens; embeddings batch jobs nightly: 3k vectors/min in EU, 2k in US.
- Many customers in EU require data to remain in EU; cross-region failover can only route EU traffic to US for certified DR cases with consent.
- Their infra uses mixed GPUs (A100 + H100 + older T4s) and SR-IOV networking. They want Redwood runtime to manage kernel selection and GPU equivalence mapping.

Reserved GPU pool proposal (SE sizing exercise 03/04):
- Active-active baseline: US-East reserved pool = 16 A100-equivalent GPUs; EU-Central reserved pool = 8 A100-eq; APAC warm standby = 4 A100-eq.
- Headroom scenarios: 20% headroom = recommended baseline; conservative plan = 30% headroom; extreme DR plan = 50% headroom (procurement requested cost delta).
- Failover strategy: weighted active-active routing with sticky sessions based on KV cache affinity; cross-region failover only for new sessions except in failover DR, to avoid KV cache cold-start penalties.
- Warm standby behavior: APAC pool kept at low-utilization, quick scale to handle 50% of APAC peak within 5 minutes; cold standby option available with longer spin up.
- Burst policy: allow +25% burstable capacity billed at overage rates; preemptible workers not allowed for customer-facing chat unless explicitly agreed.

Latency & throughput guarantees to include in SLA:
- Chat generation: p50 <= 35ms, p95 <= 160ms, p99 <= 350ms (measured from request enter to first token streamed).
- Embeddings: p95 <= 220ms per vector batch under scheduled window.
- Throughput: per-GPU sustained token/sec baseline to be established in POC; contractual per-region throughput floor with penalties if sustained drop >10% for >10 minutes.

POC plan (4 week cadence):
- Week 0: legal NDA + DPA sign, infra prep (VPC peering, firewall rules), reserve subset capacity (US 8 GPUs, EU 4 GPUs).
- Week 1: Redwood runtime deploy, model onboarding (primary + int8 quantized fallback), KV cache config and replication test across AZs.
- Week 2: Replay production traces and run synthetic spike tests (simulate AZ loss and region failover).
- Week 3: Cost-per-token analysis, latency profile, kernel selection report. Deliver final sizing scenarios (20/30/50% headroom) with pricing delta.

Commercial negotiation points:
- Prefers 12-month reserved commit with monthly billing and credits for missed SLOs (credit cap at 20% of monthly invoice).
- Wants clear, machine-measurable SLO triggers (how p95 is measured and aggregation window).
- Maintenance windows: require pre-scheduled windows with 72h notice; exclude from SLA if >=2h per month scheduled maintenance.

Security / Legal requirements:
- EU SCCs and DPA required; KMS integration with their customer-managed keys is mandatory for reserved pools.
- Need SOC2 report + network pentest summary. Security team requested a packet flow diagram for cross-region peering.

Sales notes (AE):
- Buying group: Head of Ops, SVP Product, Director of Security, CFO (procurement).
- Procurement wants three committed sizing scenarios to select headroom level. CFO explicitly asked for 10/20/30% cost sensitivities.
- Quote preference: show committed reserved fee + transparent per-minute overage for burst.

Open technical questions:
- How KV cache replication affects cold-start latency during regional failover? Need measurement plan.
- GPU equivalence mapping for customer's mixed fleet (how to credit older GPUs vs A100-eq).
- Precise egress cost modeling for cross-region failover and DR drills.

Internal risk note: Higher than average operational complexity due to active-active requirement and strict EU data residency. Risk manageable if POC validates failover behavior and KMS integration completes.
